title: Apple and rhubarb compote with yoghurt and seeds

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Every ingredient is a plain whole food or simple staple such as fruit, honey, natural Greek yoghurt, seeds and almonds.

supermarket.reason: Eating apples, forced rhubarb, an orange, Greek yoghurt, seeds and flaked almonds are all everyday Tesco lines.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a lidded saucepan and a frying pan, and the techniques are simmering and dry-toasting.

works.reason: Four apples and 300g rhubarb, simmered briefly with a little water and honey, make a sensible compote for four over 500g yoghurt, and the timings suit fruit that should hold its shape.

honest_times.reason: Peeling four apples, zesting an orange, cutting rhubarb and toasting seeds fits in 15 minutes, and the 8 plus 5 minute simmer matches the 15 cook minutes.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed item, including cinnamon, vanilla and the flaked almonds, appears in the steps, and nothing unlisted besides water is used.

seasonal_feel.reason: Stored apples form the bulk of a warm March compote, with early forced rhubarb alongside, which suits the date.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear British English with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Fruit, protein-rich Greek yoghurt and seeds make a filling, real-food breakfast a family would happily repeat.
